name: Vindemiatrix
description: A giant of type G8 III 33.6 parsecs away, 12.0 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 113226: radius 11.98 +/- 0.07 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 3.318 +/- 0.013 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 113226: mass 2.96 +/- 0.09 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 113226: effective temperature 5020 +/- 64 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 113226: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 29.76 +/- 0.14 mas, inverted

text.card: A giant of type G8 III, 34 parsecs away: 12.0 times the Sun's width and 82 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 3.318 milliarcseconds, which gives 11.98 solar radii and 5,020 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 113226: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3736865265441207424 (quality A), from 2015A&A...574A..50J; Gaia DR3 measures none
